questions.q: The editorial contrasts a stone dropped in water with a dye. What should faith be like in a believer’s life?
options: Like the water – taking any shape
Not quite. The article says: Like dye – blended into his whole being, not a separate object sitting within it.
Like the stone – solid and unchanging
Not quite. The article says: Like dye – blended into his whole being, not a separate object sitting within it.
Like dye – blended into his whole being, not a separate object sitting within it
Yes. “We take on God’s own dye.”
Like the glass – holding everything in
Not quite. The article says: Like dye – blended into his whole being, not a separate object sitting within it.
questions.rationale: “The relationship between Islam and a true believer should be like that of dye and water, not of stone and water.”

questions.q: A man asked the Prophet for something that would win him the love of both God and people. What was the reply?
options: Give gifts to God’s house and to people
Not quite. The article says: Renounce the world, and God will love you; renounce what people possess, and they will love you.
Pray much and visit people often
Not quite. The article says: Renounce the world, and God will love you; renounce what people possess, and they will love you.
Renounce the world, and God will love you; renounce what people possess, and they will love you
Right. Do not covet what is in others’ hands.
Speak well of God and of people
Not quite. The article says: Renounce the world, and God will love you; renounce what people possess, and they will love you.
questions.rationale: “If you renounce the world, God will love you; and if you renounce what people possess, they will love you.”

questions.q: The growers of Madinah stopped pollinating their date palms after a remark of the Prophet, and the crop was poor. What did he then tell them?
options: To wait another year and see
Not quite. The article says: To keep to their own methods – “You know better about your worldly affairs”.
To plant a different crop
Not quite. The article says: To keep to their own methods – “You know better about your worldly affairs”.
To ask the growers of Makkah
Not quite. The article says: To keep to their own methods – “You know better about your worldly affairs”.
To keep to their own methods – “You know better about your worldly affairs”
Well read. Proven practical knowledge is welcomed.
questions.rationale: “Then the Prophet told the date growers to adhere to their own methods, and said, ‘You know better about your worldly affairs’.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, does man need prophets although he has been given a mind?
options: Because laws change in every age
Not quite. The article says: The mind grasps what is apparent, but not unseen realities such as God and the next world.
Because most people cannot read
Not quite. The article says: The mind grasps what is apparent, but not unseen realities such as God and the next world.
The mind grasps what is apparent, but not unseen realities such as God and the next world
Yes. The prophet supplies what reason cannot reach.
Because the mind works too slowly
Not quite. The article says: The mind grasps what is apparent, but not unseen realities such as God and the next world.
questions.rationale: “This mind can only grasp things that are apparent… so far as God and the next world are concerned, they must remain forever invisible—beyond the reach of human perception.”

questions.q: How does the article describe a prophet in the Islamic sense?
options: A king appointed over his people
Not quite. The article says: A human being like others, distinguished only by being chosen as God’s messenger.
A human being like others, distinguished only by being chosen as God’s messenger
Correct. So his life can serve as an example.
A being who is more than human
Not quite. The article says: A human being like others, distinguished only by being chosen as God’s messenger.
An angel in human form
Not quite. The article says: A human being like others, distinguished only by being chosen as God’s messenger.
questions.rationale: “A prophet in the Islamic sense is no different from any other human being. His uniqueness lies simply in his being the chosen messenger of God.”

questions.q: A politician once wiped an interview from the tape with a magnet. What contrast does the article draw with the next world?
options: Records there fade with time
Not quite. The article says: Nothing recorded there can be erased or evaded; it deals only in realities.
Nothing recorded there can be erased or evaded; it deals only in realities
Right. No gadget, lawyer or friend will avail.
Recordings there are kept private
Not quite. The article says: Nothing recorded there can be erased or evaded; it deals only in realities.
Only good deeds are recorded there
Not quite. The article says: Nothing recorded there can be erased or evaded; it deals only in realities.
questions.rationale: “Search as one may, one will never find any instrument which will erase what is indelibly recorded on God’s tape.”

questions.q: The Prophet said that no one’s deeds will by themselves take him to Paradise. How does the article explain this without making deeds unimportant?
options: Deeds are required, but Paradise far exceeds their worth – it is granted by God’s mercy, not purchased
Well reasoned. To neglect deeds would be “wishful thinking.”
Deeds do not matter at all
Not quite. The article says: Deeds are required, but Paradise far exceeds their worth – it is granted by God’s mercy, not purchased.
Paradise is given by lot
Not quite. The article says: Deeds are required, but Paradise far exceeds their worth – it is granted by God’s mercy, not purchased.
Only a prophet’s deeds are counted
Not quite. The article says: Deeds are required, but Paradise far exceeds their worth – it is granted by God’s mercy, not purchased.
questions.rationale: “Paradise will not be granted to anyone without the requisite deeds, but in its ultimate sense… it is granted by the compassion of God.”

questions.q: When an atom is broken it releases far greater power. What does the article say of a person who is “broken” by defeat?
options: His hidden strength is released and he rises with new resolve
Yes. Defeat does not ruin; it awakens.
He is finished for good
Not quite. The article says: His hidden strength is released and he rises with new resolve.
He should avoid further effort
Not quite. The article says: His hidden strength is released and he rises with new resolve.
He must wait for others to rebuild him
Not quite. The article says: His hidden strength is released and he rises with new resolve.
questions.rationale: “Just as breakage does not destroy matter, so defeat does not ruin man… When man is beset by defeat, his inner forces are released.”

questions.q: The Quran calls God “Lord of the universe,” not “Lord of the nation.” What does the article read in this?
options: That each nation has its own Lord
Not quite. The article says: That Islam’s outlook is universal, not limited to one people.
That the universe has no borders
Not quite. The article says: That Islam’s outlook is universal, not limited to one people.
That Islam’s outlook is universal, not limited to one people
Exactly. And the Prophet is called a mercy for the world.
That nations are unimportant
Not quite. The article says: That Islam’s outlook is universal, not limited to one people.
questions.rationale: “This shows that Islam believes in unbounded universality and not in limitation.”

questions.q: Moses went towards a distant fire to fetch a burning brand and received prophethood instead. What does the commentary observe about such gifts?
options: They are earned by travel
Not quite. The article says: God gives a special blessing suddenly and unexpectedly, so that it is attributed wholly to Him with deep gratitude.
They are given after long notice
Not quite. The article says: God gives a special blessing suddenly and unexpectedly, so that it is attributed wholly to Him with deep gratitude.
God gives a special blessing suddenly and unexpectedly, so that it is attributed wholly to Him with deep gratitude
Well read. Not to one’s own planning.
They come only to those who ask for them
Not quite. The article says: God gives a special blessing suddenly and unexpectedly, so that it is attributed wholly to Him with deep gratitude.
questions.rationale: “When Almighty God blesses any subject of His with a special gift, He gives it suddenly and unexpectedly, so that the recipient may attribute it directly to God.”
